story.head: The Red Wings’ power play is a weapon
paras: The Flames won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in Calgary on Oct 24. The Red Wings have won two in a row, while the Flames (11-14-2) lost 5-3 to New Jersey on Friday. Going in, the Flames are sixth in the Pacific (24th in the NHL) and the Red Wings seventh in the Atlantic (tied for 25th).

The Flames’ record (.444) is about what their chances are worth. The Red Wings have played better than their record (.460) says: their chances are worth about .527, and their finishing has held them back.

The Flames play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (32nd), so the Red Wings’ power play bites, but theirs doesn’t. Calgary has scored 2.59 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Wings block more shots than almost anyone (3rd) and leave the shooting to their forwards (4th lowest), but ice the puck a lot (29th). Detroit has scored 2.60 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league.

Joel Farabee (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 27 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (7 G / 12 A / 19 P in 27 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Red Wings, Lucas Raymond (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Viktor Arvidsson (9 G / 9 A / 18 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind.

Calgary has two options in net: Devin Cooley (5-7-0 / .905 SV% in 12 GS) and Dustin Wolf (6-6-2 / .878 SV% in 14 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Cooley got the last one on Friday. Detroit also has two options: John Gibson (5-8-1 / .869 SV% in 15 GS) and Daniil Tarasov (4-4-2 / .930 SV% in 9 GS). They have split the last ten starts, and Gibson got the last one on Friday. For both teams, it’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
